These probabilities come from my prior knowledge of NAS-Bench-201 behavior, not from querying the benchmark data. The main patterns I relied on:

- Removing or weakening an edge matters less when the node's other paths already carry the signal. Conv ops on a parent edge usually reduce the marginal value of adding another conv on a related edge.
- Edits that replace the condition op itself (parent edge equals the edited edge) are the most likely to show a real interaction, since the baseline being replaced differs.
- Most pairs involve weakly coupled edges, so N is the default.
